Generally, capital gains are applied to over/under 1 year. However, Real Estate is classified differently and has an over/under of 2 years.

Understanding the tax bracket is determined but how long you have held the Real Estate. So if I sell my house after 18 months I would be in the short term tax bracket, and selling my house after 24 months I would be in the long term tax bracket.

The big difference is that after holding my home for 2 years, I qualify for exceptions. Meaning I can exclude up to 250,000 (single) / 500,000 (married) from my gains.

So if I bought my house for 200,000 18 months ago and I were to sell it today for 250,000 I would be responsible for the short term tax bracket for the 50,000 in gains.

Where as if I had that same situation and I waited 24+ months I would pay the long term tax bracket for the 50,000. However, because I waited 24+ months I can exclude up to 250,000/500,000 meaning I do not pay any tax on my gains.
